analysis_packet.certificate: The anchor couples two recency tiers with byte-bounded admission: probationary recency supplies scan resistance and first eviction priority, while protected recency preserves repeated hits and its half-capacity demotion boundary provides phase adaptation. These benefits trade off against delayed admission of newly recurring objects, possible churn under phase shifts, and byte/object hit-rate tension when object sizes differ. Capacity safety depends on exact alignment between internal byte accounting and authoritative cached membership; interface legality depends on returning only unique currently cached integer keys. Online-only visibility prevents oracle or trace-based optimization, and withheld scores leave validity obligations observable but objective superiority unverified. The history-free atomic hypothesis may improve whole-artifact coherence by avoiding anchor-relative path dependence, but its falsifier requires all-valid matched-majority and strict-median evidence, which is unavailable within this call.
obligations: Preserve the declared Policy constructor and access interface.
Maintain authoritative-state compatibility so every returned key is currently cached, unique, and an integer.
Never cause cached usage to exceed capacity_bytes, including variable-size objects and multi-eviction requests.
Use only online information available through the current access and retained legal policy state.
Remain standard-library-only and avoid benchmark, trace, oracle, networking, subprocess, and external-library dependence.
Keep cross-objective behavior coherent across object hit rate, byte hit rate, scan resistance, phase-shift adaptation, and offline-regret considerations.
Evaluate validity on the complete candidate artifact rather than relying on self-justifying edit history.
Treat comparative superiority as unestablished because scores and matched-majority evidence are withheld.
witnesses: The anchor uses probation and protected ordered states, promotes probation hits, refreshes protected hits, and demotes protected entries when protected bytes exceed half the capacity.
Insertion evicts probationary entries before protected entries, linking scan resistance and repeated-hit preservation to a direct recency tension.
Admission rejects objects larger than capacity or zero-capacity insertions, while byte accounting governs multi-object eviction.
The candidate hypothesis identifies path dependence in reversible local repair succession and proposes evaluating one complete artifact rather than an edit history.
No score, trace, oracle decision, benchmark path, or matched evaluation result is visible.
